headline: Advocacy groups present 2027 legislative priorities, including special education funding, school construction, and behavioral health access.
summary: NASW Maine, with about 950 members, named behavioral health funding and access as its top concern in a member survey. The Maine Education Association, with about 18,000 members, wants the state to keep 55% state funding for schools and wants pension improvements. The Maine School Boards Association, which represents more than 1,600 school board members, lists school construction, special education, and universal school meals among its goals. The next meeting is on November 16th, with Equality Maine and Maine Disability Rights among the groups.
discussion: Legislative priorities: Four groups described their goals for 2027, including special education funding, school construction, and literacy. Presenters said the election tomorrow could change how far these goals can go.

Medicaid billing: Presenters said school districts leave millions of federal dollars unclaimed because billing is hard. A member of the public said 2027 Medicaid changes could lower reimbursement rates, which may make billing not worth the cost.
Universal pre-K: Presenters said the state funding formula favors part-time 10-hour-a-week programs over full-day programs. They said the formula needs to be fixed.
Community schools: A community school coordinator links school needs to community services. A member of the public said community schools can also open pools, libraries, and gyms to the community.
Top priorities: When asked to name priorities, answers included special education funding, school construction, and behavioral health access.
